label: Fires only at GO, graded by observed evidence that S2 is good (a2 preferred).
short_terms: (phase == GO) * np.clip(-belief_lo, -3, 3) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S1 u")
terms: (phase == GO) * (belief < 0.5) ;; (phase == GO) * np.clip(-belief_lo, -3, 3) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 r") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") ;; (phase == GO) * (tv("action", -2) == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) * (belief < 0.5)
explanation: Active essentially only at GO (zero at D1/D2). Its magnitude tracks the ideal observer belief that S2 is the good state: clipped -belief_lo alone gives dev R^2 0.74 beyond timing. Two last-trial corrections add a little: after a rare-rewarded a1->S2 trial it is lower than belief predicts, and after a rare-rewarded a2->S1 trial higher (the model stays with the previous choice more than the ideal observer after rare rewards). Short form dev 0.77; 8-term free fit (adds prev_action, a2 S2 u, belief sign, trial-before choice) only 0.78. Future reward and since-reversal add nothing; no future variables used.

issues: The core claim holds. The feature is zero at D1 and D2 (all residuals there are about 1e-5). At GO it falls steadily across belief deciles, from +2.24 at decile 0 (sure S2 is good) to -1.98 at decile 9. Clipped -belief_lo on its own scores test R^2 0.722 (dev 0.744).

The recorded short form leaves a large systematic error. Running misses on it shows GO after 'a1 S1 u' over-predicted by -1.59, much the largest error class. The next largest is GO after 'a2 S2 u', under-predicted by +0.50. So after a common-unrewarded a1 trial the feature stays low, even though the ideal observer swings toward S2. The two rare-rewarded corrections it chose to add are smaller effects.

Replacing those two corrections with prev_action==2 and last_is('a1 S1 u') raises test R^2 from 0.754 to 0.784 (dev 0.798). That 3-term form beats the recorded 8-term free fit (test 0.764), so the claim that the free fit is near-optimal does not hold; its search was incomplete. Fitted weights: belief +0.62, prev a2 +0.45, a1 S1 u -1.58.

The explanation says both corrections lean toward repeating the previous choice. That is only partly right. The cleaner reading is a perseveration lean toward a2 after an a2 choice, plus a weak switch away from a1 after an unrewarded common a1 trial. Even after the fix, rare-rewarded trials still leave residuals: GO after a2 S1 r +0.89, after a1 S2 r -1.12. In both, the feature leans toward repeating more than the ideal observer would.
The label says nothing about the history corrections. A reader could predict the main sign from it, but not the a1 S1 u dip or the lean toward the previous choice.
